v.q: What is a servlet?
o: A Java class run by a servlet container that handles HTTP requests
A thread that the JVM creates for every HTTP connection
A build plugin that packages a web application into a WAR
A database driver that sends SQL over HTTP
v.w: A servlet is a class written against the Servlet API. The container calls it for matching requests on its own pooled threads.

v.q: Which statement about a servlet in a container is true?
o: One instance serves all requests, so it must be thread-safe
A new instance is created for every request
It is single threaded by default
It is destroyed after each response
v.w: The container normally keeps one instance and calls service() concurrently from many threads, so per-request data must not live in fields.

v.q: Which order describes the servlet lifecycle?
o: init once, service for each request, destroy once
service once, init for each request, destroy once
init for each request, service once, destroy for each request
construct, doGet, doPost, finalize
v.w: The container calls init() once, then service() for every request, and destroy() once when the servlet is taken out of service.

v.q: When is a servlet normally instantiated if loadOnStartup is not set?
o: On the first request that needs it
When the JVM starts
On every request
When the WAR is built
v.w: Without loadOnStartup the container creates the servlet lazily on the first request. loadOnStartup makes it start with the application.

v.q: What is the difference between Tomcat and WildFly?
o: Tomcat is a servlet container; WildFly is a full application server with CDI, EJB, JTA and JMS
Tomcat is a full application server; WildFly is only a servlet container
Tomcat runs only JSP; WildFly runs only EJB
There is none: both implement the same specifications
v.w: Tomcat implements the web specifications (Servlet, JSP, WebSocket). WildFly implements the whole platform including EJB, JTA and JMS.

v.q: Which of these is a servlet container but not a full Jakarta EE application server?
o: Apache Tomcat
WebLogic
Payara
WildFly
v.w: Tomcat (like Jetty and Undertow) covers the web tier only. WebLogic, Payara and WildFly implement the full platform.

v.q: How is Jakarta EE related to Java EE?
o: It is the same platform moved to the Eclipse Foundation, with packages renamed from javax to jakarta from version 9
It is an unrelated replacement written from scratch
It is only the name of the Spring integration for Java EE
It is Java EE restricted to the Web Profile
v.w: Oracle donated Java EE to the Eclipse Foundation. Jakarta EE 8 was identical, and Jakarta EE 9 renamed the packages.

v.q: Which Jakarta EE release introduced the jakarta package names?
o: Jakarta EE 9
Jakarta EE 8
Java EE 7
Jakarta EE 11
v.w: Jakarta EE 8 still used javax. The jakarta namespace arrived with Jakarta EE 9.

v.q: Why does a JAR compiled against javax.servlet fail on Tomcat 10?
o: Tomcat 10 implements jakarta.servlet, so the javax classes it expects do not exist
Tomcat 10 removed the Servlet API
javax.servlet is only for JSP
Tomcat 10 needs Java 8
v.w: The rename is binary incompatible. Libraries must be rebuilt or transformed for jakarta, which is also why Spring Boot 3 needs jakarta.

v.q: Which package was NOT renamed from javax to jakarta?
o: javax.sql
javax.servlet
javax.persistence
javax.validation
v.w: javax.sql belongs to the JDK, not to Jakarta EE, so it keeps its name. Servlet, persistence and validation moved.

v.q: What does the container do with a JSP file?
o: Compiles it into a servlet the first time it is requested
Interprets it line by line on every request without compiling
Converts it to a static HTML file at build time
Sends it unchanged to the browser
v.w: A JSP is translated into a servlet class, compiled and loaded. After that it runs like any servlet.

v.q: What is the recommended way to use JSP in an MVC design?
o: A servlet or controller prepares the model and forwards to the JSP for rendering
Put the business logic in scriptlets inside the JSP
Let the JSP read request parameters and call the database
Redirect the browser to the JSP file directly
v.w: In Model 2 MVC the servlet is the controller and the JSP is only the view. Scriptlets with logic are considered bad practice.

v.q: What is a servlet filter?
o: A component that wraps requests before and after the servlet and can modify or block them
A servlet that serves only static files
A JSP tag that removes HTML
A listener for session events
v.w: Filters form a chain around the servlet. They are used for security, encoding, compression and logging.

v.q: How do you control the order of filters declared with @WebFilter?
o: Declare the order in web.xml (the annotation does not define it)
By the alphabetical order of the class names, always
With the @Order annotation of the Servlet API
It is always the order of the Java files on disk
v.w: The Servlet API does not define an order for annotated filters. Use web.xml or register them in code.

v.q: What is the difference between forward and sendRedirect?
o: Forward stays inside the server with the same URL; redirect sends a 302 and the browser makes a new request
Forward changes the browser URL; redirect does not
Both create a new request but redirect is faster
Forward only works for POST requests
v.w: A forward is internal and keeps the request. A redirect makes the browser issue another request to a new URL.

v.q: Why use post, redirect, get after a form submission?
o: A refresh then repeats a harmless GET instead of resubmitting the form
It encrypts the form data
It is required by the HTTP specification
It keeps the session alive
v.w: Redirecting after the POST means a browser refresh repeats the GET, so the payment is not submitted twice.

v.q: How does a servlet container track an HttpSession?
o: A session id in a cookie (JSESSIONID) points to state in server memory
The whole session is stored in the cookie
The IP address of the client is the session id
The session is stored in the browser local storage
v.w: The container keeps the data on the server and sends only the session id in the JSESSIONID cookie.

v.q: Which call protects against session fixation after login?
o: request.changeSessionId()
session.setMaxInactiveInterval(0)
response.setHeader("Set-Cookie", "")
session.getAttribute("user")
v.w: Giving the user a new session id at login means an id an attacker planted before login becomes useless.

v.q: Which CDI scope gives one instance for the whole application?
o: @ApplicationScoped
@RequestScoped
@Dependent
@SessionScoped
v.w: @ApplicationScoped is the singleton scope. @Dependent, the default, creates a new instance for each injection point.

v.q: What is the default scope of a CDI bean with no scope annotation?
o: @Dependent
@ApplicationScoped
@RequestScoped
@Singleton
v.w: A bean with no scope is @Dependent: a new instance is created for every injection point, like a prototype.

v.q: What does JTA add beyond a local database transaction?
o: A global (XA) transaction across several resources such as two databases and a queue
Faster commits on a single database
Automatic retry of failed SQL
Caching of query results
v.w: JTA coordinates a two-phase commit across resources. It is slow and rarely used across microservices, where sagas are preferred.

v.q: In an EJB or a CDI bean with @Transactional, which exception rolls the transaction back by default?
o: A runtime (unchecked) exception
Every checked exception
Only an Error
None: you must always call rollback manually
v.w: By default unchecked exceptions mark the transaction for rollback and checked exceptions do not, as in Spring.

v.q: Which annotations declare a JAX-RS endpoint that reads an id from the URL?
o: @Path("/{id}"), @GET and @PathParam("id")
@RequestMapping and @PathVariable
@WebServlet and @RequestParam
@Inject and @Named
v.w: JAX-RS uses @Path, @GET and @PathParam. @RequestMapping and @PathVariable are Spring MVC.

v.q: What is JNDI used for in an application server?
o: Looking up server-managed resources such as a DataSource by name
Encrypting session cookies
Compiling JSP pages
Scheduling batch jobs
v.w: JNDI publishes resources by name, for example java:comp/env/jdbc/BankDS. The app injects them with @Resource.

v.q: Which directory of a WAR is never served directly to a browser?
o: WEB-INF
css
META-INF/resources
The root of the WAR
v.w: Everything under WEB-INF, including web.xml, classes and lib, is hidden from direct requests.

v.q: How should the Jakarta EE API dependencies be declared in Maven when deploying a WAR to an application server?
o: With provided scope, because the server supplies them
With compile scope, always bundled in the WAR
With test scope
They must not appear in the pom
v.w: The server already provides the API and its implementation, so bundling them risks class loader conflicts. Use provided scope.

v.q: How does Spring MVC relate to the Servlet API?
o: It is built on it: the DispatcherServlet is a servlet running in a container such as embedded Tomcat
It replaces the Servlet API entirely
It runs only on Netty
It needs a full Jakarta EE application server
v.w: Spring MVC runs on servlets. Only WebFlux can run without the Servlet API, on Netty by default.

v.q: Which Spring annotation corresponds to the CDI @Inject?
o: @Autowired
@Bean
@Component
@Configuration
v.w: @Autowired injects a dependency like @Inject. Spring also supports @Inject itself.
